newsitem.title: UK: London warns China of deep concern on HK lawmaking.
newsitem.headline: London warns China of deep concern on HK lawmaking.

text.p: Britain's row with China over who sets Hong Kong's laws escalated on Wednesday when Britain summoned a senior Chinese diplomat in London to warn him of "deep concerns" over the issue.

Britain says the elected Legislative Council it set up in Hong Kong should be in charge until the handover to Chinese rule on July 1. But Beijing has created a provisional legislature for the territory which will replace the elected chamber upon the handover.
Reports that this Chinese body was considering laws on public holidays in Hong Kong provoked Britain to summon the Chinese official.

Chinese official Wang Qilang "was called to the Foreign Office on 16 April and told of the British government's deep concern that the provisional legislature was seeking to operate in parallel with the Legislative Council", the Foreign Office said in a statement.
"There is only one constitutional legislature with the power to legislate in Hong Kong and that is the existing Legislative Council," it said.

"Any laws resulting from activity undertaken by the provisional legislature before July 1 would be vulnerable to legal challenge and undermine our efforts to achieve a smooth and successful transition for Hong Kong."

Beijing had already angered Britain by unilaterally setting rules on residency rights in Hong Kong after July 1. China said it would send the residency bill to the provisional legislature, rather than the current Legislative Council.
Hong Kong Governor Chris Patten said on Wednesday the China-appointed body should not be allowed to pass the residency rights legislation before July 1.
"That is our position, our position is not going to change," Patten told reporters at a public function in Hong Kong.
The Hong Kong government on Monday slammed the plan and warned that, if the bill were to be handled by the interim chamber before July 1, it would invite legal challenges.

Hong Kong's pro-democracy camp, which has been in the forefront of clashes with China over arrangements for handing the British colony back to China, opposes the interim chamber and has vowed to sue if it tries to pass laws before July 1.
